title: Marks page: pick the composition
question: The deal put three structures on the table for Transaction classification rules. Lock one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: Dual-Lens Workspace
options.lineage: bookkeeping working papers kept once per reporting lens
options.thesis: One Real/Coretax switch re-scopes the coverage strip, the mapping column, and each rule's tax badge — the page reads as one ledger per lens.
options.viewport: Lens switch and mapped/unmapped coverage on top; rule rows beneath with inline flag toggles and the active lens' mapping state; drawer-less, everything on one screen.
options.risk: A switch that moves too much becomes two pages to relearn.

options.label: Slim List + Inspector Drawer
options.thesis: A calm full-width list of one-line rule rows; selecting a rule slides in a right-side drawer holding its toggles, fiscal category, and both mapping groups.
options.viewport: Summary rows with trait chips, coverage dots and quick actions; the drawer holds full detail for the selected rule without leaving the list.
options.risk: Anything not in the row summary costs a second step, which can slow bulk review.

options.label: Expandable Rule Rows
options.thesis: Every rule is one quiet summary row that expands in place into its full sheet — flags, fiscal category, Real and Coretax mappings side by side.
options.viewport: Compact table with a traits chip cluster per row and search above; expanding a row opens a detail band with both mapping groups side by side.
options.risk: Open rows shift the table, which jars when comparing several rules at once.
